<description>
This PR speeds up the test framework’s fixed-base multiplication and Schnorr signing by:

- Changing FastGEMul to process scalars in 4-bit windows instead of individual bits. Precompute all 16 multiples for each window position, reducing multiplication from about 128 point additions on average to 64 table lookups and about 60 nonzero point additions. This trades a larger table and additional initialization work for cheaper repeated multiplications.

On my local machine (Macbook M2 Pro) the `feature_taproot.py`'s medium time decreased from 83.39s to 35.42s.
</description>

[2026-10-02] r:5391378350 review COMMENTED by fametrano (contributor):
tACK b6fc3cf0046d3106e0dfb30f320d48514eff6fb2

I checked `k * G` on this branch against a second implementation for about 10,000 random scalars plus edge cases (0, n-1, n, n+1, 2n, negative values, runs of ones, each 4-bit window position). All matched. `sign_schnorr` passes the BIP340 vectors and gave the same signatures as that implementation for 2,000 random messages and aux_rand.

On where the gain comes from: both changes matter, the window somewhat more. In my steadiest run of `feature_taproot.py` (shared machine, so rough), the window alone took about 35% off master, the cache alone about 30%, and both together 54% (62s to 29s).

Nit, not new here: no unit test multiplies G by a negative scalar. I suggested one inline.
